When a current of 0.1 mA flows, the pointer deflects by an angle of \( 30^{\circ} \). When the pointer deflects by \( 45^{\circ} \), the current flowing through is ______ \\times 10^{-4}A.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic structural diagram of a pointer-type moving-coil ammeter. The dial takes the 0 in the middle as the zero point, and there are scales such as 0.1 and 0.2 on the left and right sides; the pointer deflects relative to the middle vertical zero position, and 30° is marked in the figure. Below, it can be seen that the coil is located in the magnetic field formed by the N and S magnetic poles and the cylindrical iron core, conforming to the model of a moving-coil meter in a radial magnetic field. Reasoning: In the same ammeter, the electromagnetic torque on the coil is proportional to the current, and at equilibrium there is NBSI = kθ. Therefore, when N, B, S, and k are all unchanged, the current I is proportional to the deflection angle θ. It is known that when I1 = 0.1 mA, θ1 = 30°, and the current when θ2 = 45° is required: I2/I1 = θ2/θ1 = 45/30 = 1.5, so I2 = 0.1 mA × 1.5 = 0.15 mA = 1.5 × 10^-4 A. Therefore the blank should be filled with 1.5.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the coil-in-radial-field meter and the central zero reference, so the given deflection angles are angular displacements of the same pointer. From the text, take the calibration point I1 = 0.1 mA at theta1 = 30° and the target theta2 = 45°. Apply NBSI = k theta for the same meter, giving I2/I1 = theta2/theta1 = 45/30. Thus I2 = 0.1 mA × 1.5 = 0.15 mA = 1.5 × 10^-4 A, so the blank is 1.5.
